name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>; domain=input (lives in input.c, blocks on keyboard), descriptor accurately captures the wait-for-key loop that cycles the chapter-intro dialog panels and animates the portrait mouth-blink. No address residue; '2'/'4' frame counts are semantic dimensions, not address tails. Name matches all 6 callers (chapter-intro / shop / party-roster / promote menu input loops).
purpose: Block until a key is pressed while cycling the chapter-intro dialog panels (4 frames) and animating the portrait mouth-blink; then read and normalize the scancode via INT 16h.
logic_summary: Copies the 4-entry corner-offset table into a stack array; seeds saved_tick from the BIOS tick word and a random initial blink countdown (rng%0x32+8); sets dialog anim frame to 2 and does an initial panel render. When mode==0, blits 4 corner indicator sprites (highlighted sprite for the entry == ui_menu_cursor_idx). Then loops: on each real BIOS-tick advance (>=2 ticks, signed-wrap aware) it advances the panel frame (mod 4), re-renders, and drives the blink state machine -- when not blinking it tests the OLD countdown for 0 then decrements (==0 -> paint mouth-CLOSED sprite 3, set blinking); when blinking it paints mouth-OPEN sprite 0, reseeds the countdown (rng%0x1E+2), clears blinking. Loop exits when the keyboard buffer is non-empty. Finally sets key_input_mode=0x10 and calls int386(0x16) to fetch the scancode into last_key_pressed/key_input_mode, normalizes extended/numpad keys (0xE0 or 0x52 -> 0x1C Enter; 0x53 -> 0x01 Esc), and returns the (possibly remapped) scancode byte.

params.name: param_1
params.semantics: Render mode flag forwarded to fd2_render_chapter_intro_dialog_panels each frame; when 0 the function also blits the 4 corner cursor-indicator sprites (highlight on the entry matching ui_menu_cursor_idx).
params.reason: Live Ghidra name is the generic placeholder param_1; the value is a render-mode selector (==0 gates the corner-sprite pass and is passed through to the panel renderer). src already declares it as 'mode', which is the accurate descriptor.

returns.semantics: The pressed key's scancode byte (data_fd2_input_key_input_mode) after INT 16h read and Enter/Esc normalization; returned zero-extended.
